sn56.40:1.1: “Bhikkhus, if any bhikkhu understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,’
sn56.40:1.2: and then an ascetic or brahmin comes along—whether from the east, the west, the north, or the south—seeking an argument, searching for an argument, thinking:
sn56.40:1.3: ‘I will refute his thesis,’ it is impossible that he could make that bhikkhu shake, quake, or tremble.
sn56.40:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a stone column sixteen yards long:
sn56.40:2.2: an eight yards’ portion of it would be sunk in the ground, an eight yards’ portion above ground.
sn56.40:2.3: Even if a forceful blast of wind comes along—whether from the east, the west, the north, or the south—the column would not shake, quake, or tremble.
sn56.40:2.5: Because it has a deep base and is securely planted.
sn56.40:2.6: “So too, bhikkhus, if any bhikkhu understands as it really is ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,’
sn56.40:2.7: and then an ascetic or a brahmin comes along … it is impossible that he could make that bhikkhu shake, quake, or tremble.
sn56.40:2.12: Because he has clearly seen the Four Noble Truths.
sn56.40:2.14: The noble truth of suffering … the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
sn56.40:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
